title: Asking for directions
goal: Ask strangers for directions, understand the answer, and use the imperative — including the formal form, which works differently.
bekal: ask the way and the distance politely
understand directions given at full speed
use the informal and formal imperative

dialogs.title: Dialogo — Per andare alla stazione?
dialogs.intro: Budi is lost. Pay attention to the verb forms the man uses in his answer — that's the formal imperative.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Scusi, signore. Per andare alla stazione?
lines.id: Excuse me, sir. How do I get to the station?
lines.literal: excuse, sir. for to-go to-the station?

lines.speaker: Signore:
lines.text: La stazione? Allora, vada sempre dritto.
lines.id: The station? OK, go straight ahead.
lines.literal: the station? so, go always straight.

lines.speaker: Signore:
lines.text: Sì. Al secondo semaforo giri a sinistra.
lines.id: Yes. At the second traffic light, turn left.
lines.literal: yes. at-the second traffic-light turn to left.

lines.speaker: Signore:
lines.text: Attraversi la piazza e prenda la prima a destra.
lines.id: Cross the square and take the first right.
lines.literal: cross the square and take the first to right.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Is it far? Do I need to take the bus?
lines.literal: is far? I-must to-take the bus?

lines.speaker: Signore:
lines.text: No, no. Dieci minuti a piedi, non di più.
lines.id: No, no. Ten minutes on foot, no more.
lines.literal: no, no. ten minutes on feet, not of more.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Scusi, può ripetere? Non ho capito bene.
lines.id: Sorry, could you repeat that? I didn't quite get it.
lines.literal: excuse, you-can to-repeat? not I-have understood well.

lines.speaker: Signore:
lines.text: Dritto, sinistra al semaforo, attraversi la piazza, prima a destra.
lines.id: Straight, left at the light, cross the square, first right.
lines.literal: straight, left at-the traffic-light, cross the square, first to right.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Adesso ho capito. Grazie mille, molto gentile!
lines.id: Now I've got it. Thanks a lot, that's very kind!
lines.literal: now I-have understood. thanks thousand, very kind!

lines.speaker: Signore:
lines.text: Di niente. Buona giornata e buon viaggio!
lines.id: Not at all. Have a nice day and a good trip!
lines.literal: of nothing. good day and good trip!

notes: **Per andare a…?** is the most practical way to ask for directions. Literally "for going to…?", with no main verb at all. It's shorter and more common than a full sentence.

**The formal imperative takes the "wrong" vowel.** *-are* verbs end in *-i* (*giri!*, *attraversi!*), while *-ere* and *-ire* verbs end in *-a* (*prenda!*, *senta!*). Exactly the reverse of the normal forms. That's why street directions often sound strange even when you know the words.
**The informal imperative is easy.** It's the same as the *tu* form, except *-are* verbs end in *-a*: *gira!*, *prendi!*, *senti!*, *scusa!*.

**Scusi vs scusa** — now you know where they come from: both are imperatives of *scusare*, one formal, one informal. Likewise *senta!* (excuse me, formal) and *senti!* (hey, informal) — two words for getting someone's attention.
**Può ripetere?** is a lifesaver. Together with *può parlare più lentamente?* (could you speak more slowly?), it's your only tool when Italians answer at full speed — and they always do.
**Non ho capito** uses a past form even though it refers to now. Italians almost always say it this way, not *non capisco*. For now learn it whole; the form itself is unpacked in unit 19.

**Ordinal numbers.** *Il primo*, *il secondo*, *il terzo*, *il quarto*, *il quinto*. Used for turns, floors, and the first of the month. They agree in gender: *la prima a destra* because it refers to *la strada*.
**Di niente** = "you're welcome", alongside *prego* and *si figuri*. All three are interchangeable.

grammars.title: The imperative
body: Two columns you need to master now. The *tu* column is for friends, the *Lei* column for strangers on the street.
after: Remember the reversed pattern: **-are** formal takes *-i*, **-ere/-ire** formal takes *-a*. When in doubt, listen to officials or shop staff — they use these forms all day long.
Informal prohibitions use *non* + the infinitive: *non parlare!*, *non andare!*. In the formal form, just add *non*: *non parli!*.
The *noi* form is used as "let's" and is identical to the normal form: *andiamo!* (let's go), *mangiamo!* (let's eat), *aspettiamo!* (let's wait).

grammars.title: Words for direction and distance
after: *A due passi* literally means "two steps away" and means very close. Beware of Italian optimism about distance: *a due passi* can mean a ten-minute walk.

blocks.title: Ready-made phrases
items: *Scusi, dov'è la fermata dell'autobus?* — Excuse me, where's the bus stop?
*Quale autobus va in centro?* — Which bus goes downtown?
*Un biglietto per Firenze, andata e ritorno.* — A round-trip ticket to Florence.
*Da quale binario parte?* — Which platform does it leave from?
*Devo cambiare?* — Do I have to change?
*Quanto ci vuole?* — How long does it take?
*Mi può dire quando scendere?* — Can you tell me when to get off?

blocks.text: ⚠️ Bus and tram tickets in Italy must be **validated** in the little machine on board as soon as you get on — *timbrare il biglietto*. An unvalidated ticket counts as unused, and the fine is steep. This is the rule that catches newcomers most often.

exercises.prompt: Change these informal commands into the formal form.

items: Turn left at the traffic light.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right direction word.
items: ____ la piazza e prenda la prima a destra.
La banca è di ____ al cinema.
La farmacia è in ____ alla strada.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: Giri a destra! — Prenda la prima a sinistra! — Scusi! — Attraversi la piazza! — Senta! — Vada dritto!
Scusi, dov'è la stazione? — Vada sempre dritto. — Giri a sinistra al semaforo. — È lontano da qui? — Può ripetere? — Può parlare più lentamente?
Scusi, dov'è la stazione? — Vada sempre dritto. — Giri a sinistra. — Può ripetere? — Un biglietto per Firenze.
